Community-led · Since 2022

We go back for our own, so no one is left behind.

The Ghanaian Domestic Workers Organization is a grassroots network of Ghanaian domestic workers in Doha, supporting one another through housing crises, workplace disputes, and the everyday distance from home — and working toward formal partnership with the Ghana Embassy to do it at scale.

See our work Message us on WhatsApp
About us

Built by the community it serves.

We are not a government body or a registered charity — yet. We are Ghanaian domestic workers and volunteers in Doha who saw one another through hard moments and decided to organize. For four years we've worked informally: connecting people to emergency help, translating for those who need it, and sitting with each other through disputes that have nowhere else to go. Now we're seeking a formal welfare partnership with the Ghana Embassy to carry that work further.

Our work

Three pillars, proposed in phases.

Our concept note to the Embassy outlines a phased partnership: low-cost, immediate support first, with emergency shelter to follow once funding is secured.

Phase 1

Education & Local Orientation

"Know Your Rights" seminars, basic Arabic and cultural orientation, and plain-language education on Qatari labor law and grievance procedures — run by and for the community.

Phase 1

Counseling & Psychosocial Support

Trained, vetted volunteers offer mental health check-ins and mediation, resolving non-legal employer misunderstandings before they escalate into crises.

Phase 2

Safe Shelter & Emergency Housing

A secure temporary transit home for displaced workers, operated under Embassy coordination while legal and repatriation paperwork is processed — pending a confirmed funding and liability arrangement.

Looking ahead

Training before departure, not just after arrival.

Some of our members bring white-collar and professional backgrounds. We want to put that experience to work — building a pre-departure training program pitched directly to recruitment agencies in Ghana, so workers arrive in Qatar already prepared.

It's early-stage. If you're a recruitment agency, training partner, or funder interested in shaping it, we'd like to hear from you.

  • 01

    Pitch to recruitment agencies

    Proposals to Ghana-based agencies placing domestic and construction workers abroad.

  • 02

    Fee-based training model

    Workers pay a modest fee for pre-departure preparation, funding the program's growth.

  • 03

    Built by our own members

    Delivered by community members with professional backgrounds, currently between jobs.
